findings.rationale: railtie fixture hardcodes a backend the framework does not vendor
findings.explanation: The generated production environment names a queue backend that ships as a separate gem, so this fixture only passes where that gem happens to be installed. A backend bundled with the framework keeps the fixture self-contained.

findings.rationale: the lookup example in the doc comment now advertises the async adapter as the canonical choice
findings.explanation: Two other tables in this same file were edited to drop a row, but the prose above them still counts the adapters inline, so the numbers no longer agree with the rows beneath them.

findings.rationale: case/when ladder duplicates the adapter registry it should be reading
findings.explanation: Each removal from the registry forces a matching edit in this ladder, which is the third place the same mapping is written out. Deriving the constant from the symbol would make the ladder unnecessary.
